original: Enhance the existing URL shortener: add a max_clicks limit per link; once reached, redirects return 410 and analytics report remaining clicks.
normalized: Brownfield feature: Redirect short codes to long URLs with correct 404/410 semantics; Record and expose click analytics; Enforce a per-link click limit.
goals: Redirect short codes to long URLs with correct 404/410 semantics
acceptance_criteria: GET /{code} returns 302 to the long URL; unknown code returns 404
GET /api/v1/urls/{code}/analytics reports total clicks, last access, clicks by day and top referrers
A link with max_clicks=N redirects N times, then returns 410; analytics shows remaining clicks
All pre-existing tests still pass (no regression) and existing API fields are unchanged

ambiguities.question: What is the default, and what happens when the limit is unset?
ambiguities.assumption: Unset means unlimited (backward compatible); an exhausted link returns 410

assumptions: Unset means unlimited (backward compatible); an exhausted link returns 410
No authentication in the prototype; creation is rate-limited
